meta.title: US Product Shortlist
funnel: Pass all gates, three witnesses (tier A)
signals: 'Bought in past month' badges summed over on-target top-20 listings; listings selling 1K+/mo = sellers that actually sell.
Lifetime 'sold' of the top on-target product (keyword pages, cached).
Active US ads started 180+ days ago (category phrase or the leader's domain): someone keeps paying.
Share of Amazon top-20 units held by newcomers (listings under 500 reviews), and how many newcomers sell at all.
For the soap and sock leaders only: site traffic Jun-Sep, dated review curves, offers and economics.
meta.lede: 124 products from the corpus re-ranked by category sales on Amazon, TikTok Shop and Meta. 14 products and 5 supplements pass every gate; 5 + 3 of them are our favourites.

products.name: Turmeric glow soap
products.thesis: Established ads, traffic up 3.4× in four months, a consumable with near-zero unit cost. Reviews and traffic rise together.

reviews.label: Loox reviews per month (6,860 dated reviews, main product)

clones.phrase: active US ads with 'turmeric soap'; ~1,000 with kojic + soap

findings: Loox reviews per month: Mar 209 → Jun 484 → Sep 957 → Oct 853. The curve tracks traffic (Sep peak 913K).
44 ads still running after 180+ days; 89 after 90+ days.
96% of visitors are in the US.
Real search demand beyond ads: 'turmeric soap' 21% of 'ski boots', 'kojic acid soap' 13%.
October is ~11% below September: possibly the start of a plateau.
Trustpilot 4.8 on 367 reviews, but complaint themes are billing: double charges, held funds.
Revenue band $0.8-1.2M/mo (visits × 2-3% conversion × AOV), vs the YouTuber's $7-14M claim (~11× inflated).
risks: 'Fades / blocks pigment' is a drug claim (FDA warning letters on skin lighteners, 2022)
Meta personal-attributes policy: no 'your Black skin…'
Turmeric/kojic bars can irritate: the leader attacks 'copycats that burn'
MoCRA cosmetic duties (registration, listing, adverse events)
conditions: Cosmetic-only claims: brightens, evens the look of tone

products.name: Compression socks
products.thesis: The most proven business on the list: 190 ads alive 180+ days and two years of rising reviews. The category is huge and crowded, so we win on an angle.
products.price: Main product $34; bundles up to 8 pairs

reviews.label: Loox reviews per month (29,358 dated reviews, main product)

clones.phrase: active US ads with the exact phrase 'compression socks' (~610 of them 180+ days old)
rivals: Medical and athletic brands share the phrase
clones.read: Crowded category: the opening is an angle, not the product.

findings: Reviews grew from ≤350/mo (2024) to 2,100-2,300/mo in Jul-Sep 2026: a two-year business, not a spike.
The June 2026 review dip matches the traffic dip (387K → 226K): reviews and traffic agree.
190 ads still running after 180+ days, the most on our list.
Wide calf and nurse are proven angles: their ads survive about as long as the category average.
Men, plus size and pregnancy get tested but almost never survive 180 days: open but unproven.
October reviews −36% vs September: review-request lag or a real slowdown. Re-check in December.
risks: Crowded category (~15,000 active ads on the phrase)
Sizing and fit complaints (slipping, tight bands) on Trustpilot
conditions: A niche angle: wide calf, nurses / 12-hour shifts, men's dress
No medical claims: 'tired, swollen-feeling legs' only

products.name: Persimmon soap
products.thesis: Real, rising demand and consumable economics, but the most cloned niche on the list. Worth it only as a second bar sharing supplier, funnel and compliance with the turmeric soap.

ads.note: Swarva, the earlier leader, has 0 ads past 90 days (fading).

clones.read: Most crowded niche on the list; fake-persona pages everywhere.

findings: Trustpilot 4.7 on 750 reviews; 1-2★ only 2%; ~108 new reviews in Oct 2026.
Search for 'persimmon soap' peaked in Oct 2026.
US share unresolved: 34% (SimilarWeb, Sep) vs 71% (Hypestat, Jun-Jul).
The '97% nonenal removal' claim rests on weak public science: a 2001 Shiseido study on 22 people, a 2012 trial on 20 men.
risks: Clone flood (~2,600 ads), comparison ads already running
Customers say: too expensive, small bars, subscription cancellations
conditions: Only as the 2nd SKU of the turmeric soap brand
Possible angle: unscented or larger bars, price per wash
Check AU / CA / EU demand separately

dropped: Small category demand on Amazon and TikTok; young ads; 1-2★ share 9.5%; FDA fee
One-off purchase; fewer than 5 Amazon sellers at 1K+/mo; duty ~55%
TikTok 65K sold (PAVOI) but no Amazon sellers with badges; one-off gift; leader ~11K visits
Collagen multi-balm, retinol cream, collagen night mask (medicube, Anua), ceramide cleanser (CeraVe), work insoles (Dr. Scholl's)
Small traffic (~27K); category ~8K units/mo on Amazon
No category demand found; seasonal (judge in Dec-Feb)
Small traffic, falling; no Amazon seller at 1K+
Traffic falling 1.9M → 1.1M; category ~9.5K units/mo on Amazon
All ads under 90 days; only 2 Amazon sellers at 1K+; EPA + state registration
Lash serum, hair-growth serum, LED mask: strong demand, parked until a compliant formula or FDA-cleared OEM
blind: Amazon, TikTok and Meta were read once (7 Nov 2026). No trend except for the soap and sock leaders.
'Newcomer' = listing under 500 reviews in the top 20; DTC newcomers on Meta are not measured yet.
Cached keyword pages, date unknown; one wrong page made turmeric soap look dead.
AOV, LTV and max CAC exist for the soaps and socks; the new favourites have none yet.
Refunds, chargebacks and real margins are unknown.
next: Unit economics for every favourite: landed cost, margin, AOV, LTV, max ad cost per order
Research the leader brand for magnesium spray, scent diffuser and tallow balm (traffic, aged ads by domain, review curve)
Finish the newcomer-survival check for all favourites (Amazon blocked the run after magnesium spray)
Owner decision: supplements in or out
Samples and supplier quotes; claims review for the soaps, tallow and magnesium

favs.why: Strongest proof of all: 610 category ads aged 180+ days, 16 Amazon sellers at 1K+/mo, leader growing for two years.
favs.risk: Mature category; newcomers hold ~0% of Amazon units, so sell DTC through a proven angle (wide calf, nurses) and multi-packs.

favs.why: Leader's traffic and reviews rose together (Earthly Derm 269K → 913K visits); category confirmed: 819K sold on TikTok, Amazon 58-131K/mo. Persimmon soap = SKU 2 of the same brand.
favs.risk: Execution bet on a brand, not a category wave; cosmetic claims only.

favs.why: Most open market we measured: newcomers hold 41% of Amazon units and 4 of 5 newcomers sell. Consumable, simple formula, can be made in the US.
favs.risk: Sleep and cramp wording is a claims risk; leader brand not researched yet.

favs.why: Device + refill oils at ~$80: the best repeat model on the list. Newcomers hold 27% of Amazon units; 6 of 10 sell.
favs.risk: Only 17 Meta ads aged 180+ days: the weakest proof of the five.

favs.why: Strong in all three channels (TikTok 663K sold, 52 aged Meta ads); consumable; raw material available in the US.
favs.risk: Trend may be late-stage (not checked); newcomers hold only 2% of Amazon units.

suppFavs.why: Strongest supplement evidence: TikTok 411K sold, 210 Meta ads aged 180+ days; 9 of 10 Amazon newcomers sell.
suppFavs.risk: Heavy-metal (lead) testing and a Prop 65 warning are a must.

suppFavs.why: Broadest open market: Amazon 82K/mo with 15 sellers at 1K+, TikTok 184K sold; 8 of 9 newcomers sell.
suppFavs.risk: Low price (~$25): needs bundles or a subscription.

suppFavs.why: Corpus brand Rosabella sold 171K on TikTok; 10 Amazon sellers at 1K+; 4 of 4 newcomers sell.
suppFavs.risk: Newcomers hold only 6% of units; claims discipline.

suppGate: Supplements were outside our filters until now. To sell them: a cGMP contract manufacturer, third-party testing (Amazon requires it), and structure/function wording only. Owner decides whether this block is in.
